en.name: Croutons
en.summary: Packaged croutons keep 5–6 months in the cupboard or the refrigerator, and 11–12 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). They are dried bread with oil on them, so humidity and rancid oil are what end a bag, not bacteria.
en.pantry: A sealed bag in a cool, dry, dark cupboard keeps 5–6 months. Croutons are bread with the water baked out and oil, salt and seasoning added back, so nothing much grows in them — what finishes a bag is moisture getting in, which makes them chewy and eventually mouldy, and the oil going stale, which tastes of cardboard long before it becomes properly rancid. The bag is the seal, so clip it or decant into an airtight jar once it is open, and keep it away from the kettle.
en.fridge: 5–6 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, which is the same figure the cupboard gets — so refrigeration buys nothing here unless your kitchen is very warm, in which case the cold at least slows the oil. The fridge is humid and croutons are dry and porous, so the container must be genuinely airtight, and it should come back to room temperature before you open it. In most kitchens a sealed jar in the cupboard is the better choice.
en.freezer: 11–12 months at −18 °C (0 °F), roughly double what either the cupboard or the fridge gives. Croutons freeze well because there is almost no water left in them to form ice crystals, and they can go straight from the freezer into a salad or a soup. Bag them airtight with the air pressed out, and let the pack warm to room temperature before opening so condensation does not settle on them. A few minutes in a hot oven restores the crunch to any that have softened.
en.thawing: No thawing is needed — use them from frozen. Let a sealed pack come to room temperature before opening it, and crisp them in a hot oven if they have softened.
spoilage: Croutons that have gone chewy or leathery instead of shattering.
A stale, cardboard or rancid smell from the oil.
Mould or a musty smell in a bag that took up damp.
Insects or fine crumbs and dust at the bottom of the bag.
tips: Clip the bag or decant into an airtight jar once opened.
Refresh softened croutons in a hot oven for a few minutes.
Keep them away from the kettle and the hob.
Freeze a big bag and take out handfuls as you need them.

faq.a: 5–6 months in a sealed bag in the cupboard or the fridge, or 11–12 months frozen at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Do croutons need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No — the fridge gives the same figure as the cupboard, and it is humid. A sealed jar in a dry cupboard is simpler.
Yes, 11–12 months at −18 °C. Use them straight from frozen, and let the pack warm before opening it.

zh.name: 麵包丁（croutons）
zh.summary: 市售麵包丁放櫥櫃或冷藏都是 5～6 個月，冷凍 −18 °C 下則是 11～12 個月。它是烤乾的麵包加上油，所以終結一包的是濕氣和走油，不是細菌。
zh.pantry: 密封袋放陰涼、乾燥、避光的櫥櫃，5～6 個月。麵包丁是把水分烤掉、再加回油、鹽與香料的麵包，裡面長不出什麼東西——結束一包的是水氣跑進去（先變韌、最後長霉），以及油脂走味（在真正變成油耗之前，早就先有紙板味了）。袋子本身就是密封，所以一開封就要夾緊或倒進氣密罐，也要遠離熱水壺。
zh.fridge: 4 °C 以下 5～6 個月，和櫥櫃是同一個數字——所以除非你的廚房很熱、需要低溫拖慢油脂，否則冷藏在這裡換不到什麼。冰箱潮濕，而麵包丁又乾又多孔，所以容器必須真的氣密，而且要回到室溫才能打開。對大多數廚房來說，密封罐放櫥櫃是更好的選擇。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 11～12 個月，大約是櫥櫃或冷藏的兩倍。麵包丁很適合冷凍，因為它幾乎沒有水分可以結成冰晶，而且可以從冷凍直接丟進沙拉或湯裡。請密封裝袋、把空氣壓出，並讓整包回到室溫再打開，避免結露。軟掉的丟進熱烤箱烘幾分鐘就會恢復酥脆。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍，直接從冷凍使用。密封包要回到室溫再打開；軟掉的話用熱烤箱烘一下。
spoilage: 麵包丁變得韌韌的、咬得動，而不是入口即碎。
油脂發出陳味、紙板味或油耗味。
受潮的袋子長霉或有霉味。
袋底出現蟲或大量細碎粉屑。
tips: 開封後夾緊袋口或倒進氣密罐。
軟掉的用熱烤箱烘幾分鐘就回脆。
大包冷凍，要用時抓一把出來。

faq.a: 密封放櫥櫃或冷藏都是 5～6 個月，−18 °C 冷凍則是 11～12 個月。
不需要。冷藏和櫥櫃是同一個數字，而且冰箱潮濕。密封罐放乾燥櫥櫃更單純。
可以，−18 °C 下 11～12 個月。直接從冷凍使用，整包要回溫再打開。
